🤖 **QA AI-generated AC — From SL: ZI-510 — TNT Express label fail when product name contains '&' or exceeds length [#387029]**

### Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1:** Given a TNT Express shipment where the Shopify product name contains an ampersand (e.g., "Books & Stationery"), when the merchant generates a label from the ORDERS tab, then the label is created successfully and no API error is returned from TNT Express.

- **AC2:** Given a TNT Express shipment where the product name contains an ampersand, when the label is generated successfully, then the TNT request payload must not contain the literal string `&` in either the `pieceReference` or `goodsDescription` fields — the ampersand must be stripped or replaced with a safe equivalent before the XML is submitted.

- **AC3:** Given a TNT Express shipment where the product name contains other XML-unsafe characters (e.g., `<`, `>`, `"`, `'`), when the merchant generates a label from the ORDERS tab, then the label is created successfully and no XML-encoding artefact (e.g., `<`, `>`, `"`) appears literally in the `pieceReference` or `goodsDescription` fields of the outbound TNT request.

- **AC4:** Given a TNT Express shipment where the product name exceeds the maximum allowed character length for `pieceReference` or `goodsDescription`, when the merchant generates a label, then the label is created successfully and the field value is truncated to the permitted length after sanitization (sanitize first, then truncate — not the reverse).

- **AC5:** Given a TNT Express shipment where the product name contains both an ampersand and a length that exceeds the field limit (e.g., "Books & Stationery Supplies International Edition Extra Long Title"), when the merchant generates a label, then the label is created successfully, the ampersand is sanitized, and the resulting value is truncated to the permitted length — confirming the sanitize-then-truncate order is respected.

- **AC6:** Given a TNT Express shipment where the product name contains no special characters and does not exceed the field length limit, when the merchant generates a label, then the label is created successfully and the `pieceReference` and `goodsDescription` values in the TNT request exactly match the product name (no unintended modification).

- **AC7:** Given a TNT Express label generation attempt that previously failed with a TNT API error due to an ampersand in the product name (reproducing the customer-reported broken state), when the fix is applied and the merchant retries label generation for the same order from the ORDERS tab, then the label is generated successfully and a label artifact (PDF or ZPL) is available for download.

- **AC8:** Given any TNT Express label generation scenario (with or without special characters), when the label generation fails for any reason unrelated to this fix (e.g., invalid address, missing weight), then the existing error message and failure behaviour are unchanged — the sanitization logic must not suppress or alter unrelated TNT API error responses.

**Analysis completed** (sl-iteration analyze)

**Confidence**: HIGH
**Status**: 📝 READY FOR DEV

**Root Cause Identified**:
TNT request builder passes raw `productName` into `pieceReference` and `goodsDescription` with only length-slicing — no special-character sanitization — so `&` reaches the XML body and js2xmlparser escapes it to `&` before the post-process CDATA wrap runs, sending `&` literally to TNT (and `goodsDescription` has no CDATA wrap at all).

**Key Files**:
- `server/src/shared/API/carriers/tnt/tntRequestBuilder.js:649-668` (buildAndReturnPieceData)
- `server/src/shared/API/carriers/tnt/tntRequestBuilder.js:14-19` (replaceSpecialCharacters helper — already exists, used only for postcodes)
- `server/src/shared/storepepHelperFunctions.js:132` (fixToMaxCharacters — pure slice, no escaping)

**Implementation**: Small, file-local. Sanitize `pieceReference` and `goodsDescription` before js2xmlparser; reuse `replaceSpecialCharacters` or a TNT-narrow `& < > " '` sanitizer; keep length cap order = sanitize→truncate. Consider the new `attributesToSanitize` config pattern from commit `2f9e7fdb`. Add Jest unit tests.

⚠️ Per-file blast-radius maps had no entries for `tntRequestBuilder.js` — analysis is derived from direct code reading.

[Feature] WooCommerce Product Bundle — Line Item Classification & Packaging

---

**Description**

Customers reported that the aggregate weight setting configured on their bundle products in WooCommerce was not being respected in StorePep.

As part of fixing this, WooCommerce Product Bundle orders previously sent all line items (parent + components) into packaging. This feature correctly classifies each line item and filters packaging based on how the bundle is configured in WooCommerce:

- Assembled bundle (components not shipped individually) — Bundle parent is packed, components are excluded
- Unassembled bundle (all components ship individually) — Components are packed individually, bundle parent is excluded
- Regular products in the same order — Unaffected, packed as normal

**Test Scenarios**

- Assembled bundle — Bundle parent only, no components
- Unassembled bundle — Components only, no bundle parent
- Assembled + preserve weight — Bundle parent only, verify weight includes component weights
- Assembled + quantity > 1 — Bundle parent with correct quantity, no components
- Assembled + one component set to ship individually — Bundle parent + that component only
- Assembled + ship individually + price individually — Components only, each with their own price
- Assembled + price individually — Bundle parent only, components priced individually on invoice
- Assembled + price individually + discount — Same as above, verify discount is reflected correctly in prices
- Assembled bundle + normal product — Bundle parent + normal product, no components
- Unassembled bundle + normal product — Components + normal product, no bundle parent

**Theme:** Service-point selection and automation behavior
**Pain:** 10/10 | **SLA:** Breached

**Core broken behavior:** The PostNord automation action `Set Default Service Point` is overwriting an already selected customer checkout service point because the automation logic always writes the nearest service point into `order.localPickupLocation.*` instead of treating the action as a fallback.

**Fixed behavior target:** If the order already contains a customer-selected PostNord service point, MCSL must preserve that value during label generation. The default-service-point action must run only when the order has no selected service point.

**Analysis-grounded implementation scope:** The latest analysis identifies `setDefaultServicePointForPostNord` as the override point and traces the customer selection to the same order fields used later by automation. The implementation is a precedence guard, not a redesign of the service-point flow.

**Customer-specific grounding:** Maustemesta reproduced this on order #33295, where the buyer-selected service point was replaced by the nearest one. The earlier support workaround of removing the automation rule also broke the fallback path for orders with no customer-selected service point.

**Out-of-scope note:** The empty catch block flagged in the analysis is explicitly follow-up work and should not be treated as part of this fix scope.

**Blast radius:** PostNord service-point label generation with the default-service-point automation action enabled. The no-selection fallback must continue to work, and unrelated carrier automation must not regress.

**Verification focus:** customer-selected SP precedence, fallback-only automation behavior, successful label generation when no SP was chosen, and no return to the earlier “disable rule and break fallback” misdiagnosis path.

- AC1: Given a Shopify MCSL store has the `Set Default Service Point for PostNord` automation action enabled and an order already contains a customer-selected PostNord service point from checkout, when the merchant generates the label, then the customer-selected service point is preserved and used for the shipment.

- AC4: Given the merchant previously followed the workaround of removing the automation rule and encountered failures on orders with no selected service point, when this fix is deployed and the automation rule remains enabled, then the fallback path still works for orders without a service-point choice and no longer forces the merchant to choose between fallback and customer choice.
- AC5: Given the Maustemesta reproduction path for order #33295 or an equivalent scenario is re-tested, when the order carries a buyer-selected service point, then the generated label uses that exact selected pickup point instead of the nearest fallback point.

**Status**: 📝 READY FOR DEV

`setDefaultServicePointForPostNord` at `AutomationActionsManager.js:465-503` unconditionally overwrites `order.localPickupLocation.*` with the nearest service point. No check for whether the customer already chose an SP at Shopify checkout — that selection lands in the same fields via `shopifyToStorepepOrderMapper.js:306-309` and gets silently clobbered. The rule was designed as a fallback but behaves as an override.

STORY CARD — TNT Australia: Fallback Rates

PR: [https://bitbucket.org/xadapter-cyd/storepep-react/pull-requests/3027](https://bitbucket.org/xadapter-cyd/storepep-react/pull-requests/3027 "smartCard-inline")
Feature Area: Carrier Configuration / Checkout Rates
Platform: Shopify, WooCommerce
Carrier: TNT Australia

## CUSTOMER REQUIREMENT

TNT Australia's shipping API goes down intermittently. When this happens,
buyers at checkout see no shipping options and cannot complete their order —
causing lost sales for the merchant.

Merchants need a way to pre-configure static fallback shipping rates so that
checkout always shows at least one shipping option, even when TNT Australia
is completely unavailable.

The fallback must:

- Be configured from carrier services.
- Appear at checkout transparently — the buyer sees a normal shipping option
  with the merchant's chosen name and price
- Be visible in the StorePep order summary after the order is placed, so the
  merchant knows which fallback service the buyer selected

## CARD DESCRIPTION

This feature adds a Fallback Rates section to the TNT Australia carrier
settings panel. Merchants can define one or more static services (display name

- price) that are served to checkout automatically whenever the TNT Australia
  API fails.

End-to-end flow:

- Merchant configures fallback services in Settings → Carriers → TNT Australia
- Buyer checks out; TNT Australia API fails
- StorePep detects the failure and serves the static fallback rates instead
- Buyer selects a fallback service and places the order
- Order arrives in StorePep; the FB: prefix on the shipping code identifies it
  as a fallback order
- StorePep resolves the selected carrier/service and stores it on the order
- Order summary panel → Rate Summary section shows the customer's selected
  service under "Customer Selected"

## ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA

NOTE: Feature toggle "carriers.tntAustralia.fallbackRates.enabled" must be ON
for the test account for all tests below (except AC-7 which tests the toggle).

## AC-1: Fallback Rates Configuration UI

Go to Settings → Carriers → TNT Australia → open carrier settings
→ A "Fallback Rates" section is visible below the service rename table

Observe the section with no rates configured
→ Shows "Enable Fallback Rates" checkbox and "No fallback services
  configured" message

Check the "Enable Fallback Rates" checkbox
→ Checkbox becomes checked

Click "+ Add Service"
→ A new row appears with: Service (dropdown), Display Name (text),
  Rate (number), Currency (default AUD)

Select a service from the dropdown
→ Service code populates; Display Name auto-fills with the service name

Override Display Name with a custom value (e.g. "TNT Express")
→ Custom name is accepted

Enter a rate (e.g. 12.50)
→ Decimal values accepted

Click "+ Add Service" again
→ Second row added; both rows independently editable

Click × on the second row
→ Row removed; first row remains

Click Save with an empty Service dropdown on a row
→ Red border on the Service field; save is blocked

Click Save with an empty Rate field on a row
→ Red border on the Rate field; save is blocked

Fill all required fields and Save
→ Saves successfully; data persists on page reload

Uncheck "Enable Fallback Rates" and Save
→ Checkbox persists as unchecked on reload; configured rates NOT deleted

## AC-2: Fallback Rates Served at Checkout

TNT Australia API fails; buyer proceeds to checkout on connected store
→ Checkout shows configured fallback service(s) with merchant's display
  name and rate

Verify what the buyer sees
→ Display Name (e.g. "TNT Express") and Rate (e.g. $12.50 AUD) match
  what was configured

TNT Australia API is working normally
→ Real TNT rates appear; fallback rates are NOT shown

fallbackEnabled = false on the carrier; TNT API fails
→ No TNT rates at checkout (same as pre-feature behaviour)

## AC-3: Order Import — Shopify

Buyer selects a fallback rate at Shopify checkout and completes the order
→ Order imports successfully into StorePep

Check the shipping method code on the imported order
→ Shows the bare rule ID (e.g. 76|TNT|2) — the "FB:" prefix is stripped

Rate Summary behaviour covered in AC-5

## AC-4: Order Import — WooCommerce

Buyer selects a fallback rate at WooCommerce checkout and completes order
→ Order imports successfully into StorePep

Same checks as AC-3.2 and AC-5
→ Same expected results

## AC-5: Rate Summary — "Customer Selected" Display

Open a fallback order in StorePep → order summary panel → Rate Summary
→ An entry labelled "(Customer Selected)" appears with the carrier name
  and the service the buyer chose

Verify the entry content
→ Carrier name, carrier type, and service name all match the configured
  fallback rate that was selected at checkout

Open a normal (non-fallback) order
→ Rate Summary shows automation rules as usual; NO "Customer Selected"
  entry is present

Open the fallback order summary multiple times (reload, re-open)
→ "(Customer Selected)" appears every time; no duplicate entries

## AC-6: Checkout Failure Banner

TNT Australia checkout rates return empty (no rules matched)
→ A persistent banner appears in StorePep:
  "Checkout rates are failing for TNT Australia — buyers are seeing
   no shipping options."

Dismiss the banner
→ Banner disappears

Another checkout failure occurs within 10 minutes
→ Banner does NOT re-appear (throttled per account for 10 minutes)

Wait 10+ minutes, then trigger another failure
→ Banner appears again

Feature toggle OFF for the account, TNT rates fail
→ No banner shown

KNOWN BEHAVIOUR: On the first checkout failure after a server restart, the
banner may appear up to 3 times simultaneously. This is a known cosmetic issue
(Shopify sends 3 concurrent rate requests; all read the throttle as zero before
any writes). Does not affect rate serving or orders. Dismiss all instances —
subsequent failures within 10 minutes will be correctly suppressed.

## AC-7: Feature Toggle Gate

Feature toggle OFF for the account
→ Fallback Rates section is NOT visible in TNT Australia carrier settings

Feature toggle OFF, TNT API fails at checkout
→ No fallback rates served; same behaviour as before this feature

Feature toggle ON for the account
→ Fallback Rates section appears in TNT Australia carrier settings

## AC-8: Other Carriers Not Affected

Open any non-TNT-Australia carrier settings
→ No Fallback Rates section visible

Import a normal order from any other carrier
→ Rate Summary shows no "Customer Selected" entry

Checkout rates for FedEx / UPS / DHL etc.
→ No change in behaviour

## OUT OF SCOPE

- Fallback rates for carriers other than TNT Australia
- Automatic price adjustment (rates are static; must be updated manually)
